findings.source_passage: The short-hand writers, the reporters of the court, and the reporters of the newspapers invariably decamp with the rest of the regulars when Jarndyce and Jarndyce comes on. Their places are a blank.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Who happen to be in the Lord Chancellor's court'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a critically noticed ironic aside — the press literally vacates when Jarndyce and Jarndyce is called, leaving 'a blank'; the phrase 'Their places are a blank' is rhetorically and interpretively distinctive, underlining institutional meaninglessness. Its absence removes a key satirical beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence verbatim: 'The short-hand writers, the reporters of the court, and the reporters of the newspapers invariably decamp with the rest of the regulars when Jarndyce and Jarndyce comes on. Their places are a blank.' Insert it before the description of the little mad old woman.

findings.source_passage: leaden-headed old obstruction, appropriate ornament for the threshold of a leaden-headed old corporation, Temple Bar
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The raw afternoon is rawest'
findings.why_it_matters: The deliberate repetition of 'leaden-headed' (applied first to the physical gateway, then to the corporation) is a signature rhetorical figure; the draft drops the second clause entirely, losing the satirical doubling that critics highlight as Dickens's institutional critique in miniature.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'leaden-headed old obstruction, appropriate ornament for the threshold of a leaden-headed old corporation, Temple Bar.'

findings.source_passage: fog in the eyes and throats of ancient Greenwich pensioners, wheezing by the firesides of their wards; fog in the stem and bowl of the afternoon pipe of the wrathful skipper, down in his close cabin
findings.why_it_matters: The accumulating fog-catalogue's rhythm depends on each item's specific scenic detail ('wheezing by the firesides of their wards'; 'down in his close cabin'); the draft strips these phrases, reducing the anaphoric list to bare nouns and losing the claustrophobic texture Dickens builds deliberately.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full phrases: 'Fog in the eyes and throats of ancient Greenwich pensioners, wheezing by the firesides of their wards; fog in the stem and bowl of the afternoon pipe of the wrathful skipper, down in his close cabin.'

findings.source_passage: Shirking and sharking in all their many varieties have been sown broadcast by the ill-fated cause
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'How many people out of the suit'
findings.why_it_matters: The source's nominalized, alliterative formulation ('Shirking and sharking in all their many varieties') is rhetorically distinctive; the draft's 'shirkings and sharkings have been sown broadcast' strips the appositive and slightly garbles the voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'Shirking and sharking in all their many varieties have been sown broadcast by the ill-fated cause.'

summary: The draft is largely faithful but omits the signature 'Their places are a blank' sentence (a critically noted ironic aside marking the press's abandonment of Chancery), drops the rhetorically doubled 'leaden-headed old corporation' phrase at Temple Bar, and strips the fog catalogue of its specific scenic detail — the high-severity absence alone warrants regeneration.
